<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:intro-product-expansion}
    A collection $(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_D)$ is \emph{$\nu$-product expanding} if every $c\in\mathcal{C}_1\boxplus\cdots\boxplus~\mathcal{C}_D$ has a representation $c=\sum_{i=1}^D a_i$, where $a_i\in\mathcal{C}^{(i)}$, such that
    \[
        \nu\sum_{i=1}^D\left\Verta_i\right\Vert_i\leq\left\Vertc\right\Vert_H.
    \]
    The collection is \emph{two-sided $\nu$-product expanding} if both $(\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_D)$ and $(\mathcal{C}_1^\perp,\dots,\mathcal{C}_D^\perp)$ are $\nu$-product expanding.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:KP25 main thm}
    Fix $D\geq1$ and intervals $I_1,\dots,I_D\subseteq(0,1)$ with nonempty interior. There exists $\nu>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there are codes $\mathcal{C}_1,\dots,\mathcal{C}_D\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{2^{t_n}}^n$, where $t_n=(n+1)^D$, with $\dim(\mathcal{C}_i)/n\in I_i$ such that the collection is two-sided $\nu$-product expanding.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:intro-main}
    Fix $D\geq1$ and $0<\rho<1/2$. There are constants $\nu>0$ and $n_0$, depending only on $D$ and $\rho$, such that the following holds. For every $n\geq n_0$ and integers $k_1,\dots,k_D$ satisfying $\rho n\leq k_i\leq(1-\rho)n$, there is a prime
    \[
        p=O\!\left(2^{n^D}n^D\log n\right)
    \]
    such that independent uniformly random codes $\mathcal{C}_i\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^n$ of dimensions $k_i$ are two-sided $\nu$-product expanding with probability at least $1-1/\log(n+1)$. The constant in the field-size bound depends only on $D$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
